name: Shroud an area
summary: An always-on field around the unit keeps the nearby ground dark for the enemy team: nothing inside shows on their screens or minimap, so the unit and the teammates beside it are hidden from watchers and scouts outside. It is a rule about vision, not invisibility: an enemy who walks into the field sees whatever lies within its own sight as usual, and the darkness closes again once it leaves or dies. The field travels with its carrier, which is usually fragile and unarmed. Unlike cloak, detectors do not undo it, because it hides by vision, not stealth; whether an attack from inside gives the shooter away differs (League of Legends brush briefly exposes an attacker); unlike smoke, it blinds only the enemy; unlike jamming, it hides from eyes, not just from radar and locks.
counterplay: Send a scout, or any unit, into the field: it sees everything within its own sight there, and the dark closes behind it only after it leaves.
Find and kill the carrier: it is fragile and unarmed, and the field goes with it.
Treat a dark patch as a warning: something is under it, so prepare where it is heading.
Scan it or fire area weapons blind into it; a reveal lights it up at least for a moment.

other_examples.note: The fixed version the truck copies: while it stands and has power, the building keeps a patch of ground around itself under shroud for the enemy. An enemy unit passing through lifts the shroud only near itself, and it settles back behind it. Computer opponents ignore shroud altogether, so it only fools human players.

sources.title: Gap generator (Red Alert 1), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.version: Red Alert with Counterstrike and The Aftermath
sources.note: Its quote box copies the Red Alert manual's Gap Generator entry. Read from the copy-check page cache (copy fetched 2026-10-20).

other_examples.note: A powered base building that keeps a wide circle under shroud for everyone but its owner and allies, renewing it all the time: a spy plane pass or a psychic reveal shows what is under it for only a moment, and it blocks the enemy's spy satellite. An enemy unit inside sees only its close surroundings, which go dark again once it moves on. Unpowered or destroyed, it stops, and the ground can be uncovered as usual.

sources.title: Gap generator (Red Alert 2), Command & Conquer Wiki
sources.version: Red Alert 2, also its Yuri's Revenge expansion

shooter_analogues.note: Patches of tall grass in this top-down action game hide every unit inside from enemies outside, as if in fog of war, until the enemy gains sight inside it by walking in or placing a ward. It is not stealth, and attacking from inside exposes a small area for a moment. One champion, Ivern, can create new brush with an ability.

In this top-down team shooter, Sandy throws a sandstorm over a large area for several seconds; he and his allies inside become invisible to enemies, except to enemies who come within a short distance. A star power that makes the storm hurt enemies also gives their positions away through its damage ticks.

player_translation.summary: A fragile support unit, usually unarmed, that carries darkness with it: the ground around it stays black for the enemy team, so the teammates moving with it cannot be seen coming. The enemy sees inside only by walking in.
as_user: Drive with your team's push: the enemy sees only a dark patch moving on the map, not what is in it, so they cannot read the size or make-up of the attack until it arrives.
Park beside a flank, an objective or a revive to hide what is there; the field is always on, with no key to press.
You have no gun, so your skill is positioning: stay in the middle of your escort, inside the dark, out of the enemy's reach.
Your field blinds enemy scouts and long-range spotting from outside, so their artillery and snipers have nothing to aim at.
as_target: A moving black patch on the ground and the minimap is itself the warning: something is in there.
To see inside, send someone in; whoever enters sees only within their own sight, and the dark closes again behind them.
Shell the patch blind with area weapons, or scan it: a reveal lights it up at least for a moment.
Find the carrier and kill it; it is fragile and cannot shoot back, and once it dies the field lifts.
teammates: Escort dependency: the carrier needs teammates around it, and they need it to stay hidden.
Bait and trap: a dark patch near an objective may hide a full squad or nothing at all, so the enemy must commit someone to check.
On the enemy team, scouts and reveal abilities become key picks.
controls: No key: the field is always on and follows the unit (passive), so it spends none of the tier's key budget.
The pure version has no weapon and uses only movement and the universal keys; variants may add Q to switch the field off for speed, or to throw a short-lived blackout elsewhere.
feedback: Seen by the enemy, the field is drawn as black shroud with a soft edge, on screen and on the minimap, and units inside are not drawn.
The owner's team sees a faint team-coloured ring at the field's edge, so allies know where they are hidden.
An enemy inside sees its own sight circle cut out of the dark.
A low hum and a turning dish on the carrier when seen up close.
changes_from_rts: Red Alert 1 has no fog of war (explored ground stays in view), so shroud is the only way to hide there; a team shooter has fog and shared sight, so the field must block the enemy's shared vision, long sight and minimap into the area from outside.
Red Alert 1's computer players ignore shroud entirely; here every player and every bot obeys the same vision rules, so the field always works.
The truck has no weapon at all; an unarmed player unit needs enough speed or toughness to survive, or a light self-defence weapon, to be fun to play.
A field that hides a large army is too strong in a team shooter; size it to hide a small squad around the carrier.
The darkness must look deliberate on screen (a clear moving patch), so enemies know there is something to scout rather than thinking vision is broken.

team_play.notes: The field is worth only as much as the teammates it hides: the carrier needs an escort and the escort needs the carrier, while the enemy must spend a scout, a reveal or a blind barrage to learn what is inside.

notes: Needs per-team fog of war that a field can override, on screen and on the minimap, decided on the server so no client ever receives the hidden units.
Sight rules for overlaps: an enemy inside sees within its own sight, allies always see, and reveals pierce the field for a moment.
A moving dark patch must render from above so it reads as a deliberate field, not missing graphics.
Bots, auto-targeting and lock-ons must respect the field (Red Alert 1's AI simply ignored it).
Too large a field hides whole armies and removes the information game; keep the radius to a squad.
Several carriers together can black out a whole lane.
Combined with cloak or disguise, a team can become impossible to find, so the generator keeps cloak off the same card.
Too fragile and the carrier dies on sight; too tough and it is a free invisibility aura.
Missing information is hard to read: players must understand that a black patch is a field, not a bug.
Allies must know they are hidden and where the edge is.
Enemies inside must see clearly what their own sight shows.

variants.name: Escort field
variants.summary: The base form: an always-on field around the carrier that hides it and nearby allies and moves with it.

variants.name: Fixed generator
variants.summary: Deploy into a stationary generator that casts a wider field while planted; pack up to move again.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 1 and 2 Gap Generator buildings, static and wider than the truck's field

variants.name: Thrown blackout
variants.summary: On a key, throw a device that keeps an area dark for the enemy for several seconds, hiding allies who stand in it.
variants.seen_in: Brawl Stars Sandy's Sandstorm; the wiki guesses that a cut Radar Jammer ability of the Generals Radar Van would have obscured an area

variants.name: Reveal-resistant
variants.summary: The field renews itself constantly: scans and spotting passes show what is inside for only a moment before the dark returns.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Gap Generator against spy planes and the psychic reveal

variants.name: Grown cover
variants.summary: On a key, grow a patch of tall cover that hides whoever stands in it from enemies outside until they walk in.
variants.seen_in: League of Legends Ivern creating brush

variants.name: Blackout reset
variants.summary: A one-shot that wipes the enemy team's map knowledge (last seen positions, explored ground), forcing them to scout again.
variants.seen_in: Red Alert 2 Spy getting into a radar building resets the shroud for that player

adds_strengths.why: Hides itself and nearby teammates from enemies watching from outside, so the enemy cannot read a push until it arrives.

adds_weaknesses.why: A moving dark patch tells the enemy that something is coming, and anyone who walks in sees what is there.

counters.why: Scouts watching from outside the field see only darkness.
Long-range guns that rely on spotters find no targets under the field.
Long sight shows nothing inside the field.

countered_by.why: A scan lights up the field and everything under it, at least for a moment.
Fast flankers dive into the field, see what is there and hunt the fragile carrier.
Area fire into the dark patch hits whatever hides there without needing to see it.

open_questions: With fog of war, what exactly does the field block: the enemy's shared vision and minimap into it, or also an enemy's own sight from just outside? (Recommended: everything seen from outside the field; an enemy inside sees within its own sight.)
Should a reveal pierce the field fully, briefly, or not at all? Red Alert 2's gap generator lets a reveal show it for only a moment.
Should the carrier be armed at all? The source unit has no weapon.

The field is always on, which the word lists normally give to a sensor trait; should a sensor-trait twin be added, leaving this pattern for the on-key variants? The source unit's fit notes ask for one.
Should an attack from inside the field give the shooter away for a moment, as an attack from League of Legends brush does? The gap generator pages say nothing about firing from under the field.

shooter_fit.reason: Vision denial works in top-down games with fog of war (League of Legends brush, Brawl Stars' Sandy), but an unarmed carrier is hard to make fun, and the effect needs very clear presentation and server-side vision.
